newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Energy says has pre-paid royalties.
newsitem.headline: FCL Energy says has pre-paid royalties.

text.p: Fletcher Energy said on Tuesday it had prepaid Mobil Oil Corp the remaining royalty payment obligation of NZ$225 million arising from the 1993 sale of Fletcher Energy's methanol assets.
This figure is the net present value of the remaining monthly payments scheduled under a royalty agreement ending in 2003.
The obligation arose from the sale of methanol assets, including a synthetic petrol plant to Methanex Corp in 1993.
Under the agreement, royalties were payable to Mobil for the gas-to-gasoline technology. Fletcher made a provision in its 1992/93 accounts and has been reducing it each year as payments were made.
The timing of the prepayments results in the elimination of the provision and produces a gain of NZ$37 million in the 1996/97 accounts.
As well, an after-tax change of $19 million will be taken on the company's Flour Bluff gas field in the U.S.
FCL Energy said the prepayment will free cash flow by approximately NZ$28 million annually until 2002 and $8 million in 2003.
The increase arises from the end of royalty payments offset by the interest charge on the debt required to fund the prepayment.
